options.title: shared/pkg/aiclient + AIService in ms-system-setting (the repo's own T-F3-18 path)
options.summary: Build the AI foundation where the project's decom ledger already says it belongs: a new provider-agnostic `shared/pkg/aiclient` (OpenAI-compatible, netguard-guarded, retry + key redaction) plus an `AIService` in ms-system-setting that resolves the model per org/project, stores conversations as header + turns, enforces a per-organization budget, and serves `/ai/conversation/*` behind `AI_ENABLED`. Keys stay sealed in system-setting and only leave over svcauth-signed internal gRPC, so BL-H02 reuses the same contract.
options.approach:
**Shape**: exactly the path the repository's own solution names — `backend/specs/crs/v4/solutions/SOL-P3c-E_files-ai-f18-f24.md:46-96` (T-F3-18) and `tools/conformance/retired_services.yaml:220` (`replaced_by: F24 … qua shared/pkg/aiclient`). `backend/shared/pkg/aiclient` does not exist yet (verified by glob), so this is new code, not a refactor.

1. **`backend/shared/pkg/aiclient` (new)**: `Client.Chat/Stream`, `New(Provider{Name,BaseURL,APIKey,Model,Params})`, one OpenAI-compatible transport (`POST <api_url>/chat/completions`, `Authorization: Bearer`) serving the three providers the SPA can actually create (`Open AI`, `DeepSeek`, `ZhiPu AI` — `ui/tms/src/enums/modelEnum.ts`); `Claude`/`Bedrock` return `ErrProviderUnsupported` → HTTP 422 and stay a documented deferred line, never a stub. Transport = `netguard.NewClient(netguard.FromEnv(netguard.AdminTarget), 60s)` — the four profiles already exist (`backend/shared/pkg/netguard/netguard.go:41-57`) and `AdminTarget` is the profile NFR-SE-05/ADR-15 assign to admin-configured destinations. 2 retries on 429/5xx/408 honouring `Retry-After`; input/output caps (`AI_MAX_INPUT_CHARS`, `AI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`); `ai_requests_total{provider,model,status}`, `ai_latency_seconds`, `ai_tokens_total`; every error string and log line scrubbed of the key (NFR-SE-04).
2. **`AIService` in ms-system-setting**: `ResolveModel` / `ListMessages` / `AppendTurn`. Model pick: project → organization → system default, only `status=enabled`; `PERSONAL` ⇒ owner, `SYSTEM`+`PUBLIC` ⇒ any signed-in user, `PRIVATE` ⇒ owner/admin, comparing `owner_type` after `TrimSpace` (the UI enum ships `"SYSTEM "` with a trailing space). Keys are opened with the existing `internal/secret` (`Seal/Open/Show/Resolve`, `internal/secret/secret.go:21-50`, already used by `internal/usecase/ai/ai.go:36,134`) and leave the service only over an `svcauth`-signed internal gRPC `AIService` (`backend/shared/pkg/svcauth`) with `RequireCaller("case-management","api-test")`, so BL-H02 never reads `ai_model_source` cross-service (ADR-06).
3. **Data — `migrations/V037__ss_ai_conversation_v2.sql`** (V036 is the current head): extend `ai_conversation` (`title`, `scene`, `organization_id`, `project_id`, `model_id`, `update_time`, index on `(user_id, update_time)`), add `ai_conversation_message` (`conversation_id`, `role`, `content`, `tokens_in/out`), add `ai_org_usage` (`organization_id`, `period`, `requests`, `tokens_in/out`, `cost`). Register the new tables under system-setting in `backend/db/ownership.yaml:33` so `dbown` stays green (ADR-06).
4. **Routes** in `internal/handler/ai/conversation.go`, mounted from `internal/handler/router.go` (today only `/system/ai-config/*`, `/system/ai-conversation/*`, `/ai/config/*` exist — lines 342-361): `/ai/conversation/{add,chat,update,list,delete/:id,chat/list/:id}`, shaped to `ui/tms/src/api/modules/ai.ts`. `add` must be idempotent on the client-sent `conversationId` and `chat` must upsert, because the SPA fires `addChat` without awaiting it. Status contract: `AI_ENABLED=false` ⇒ 503, no model configured ⇒ 422, provider failure ⇒ 502 with the real scrubbed message, org over budget ⇒ 429 + `Retry-After`; the budget read and `AppendTurn` run in one transaction. `AI_ENABLED` follows the `NOTIFICATION_SSE_ENABLED` precedent (`internal/config/config.go:19-20,109`). Legacy `/system/ai-conversation/*` is left in place.
5. **Gateway**: `/ai/conversation/*` is proxied today to the retired ai-agent-service (`backend/services/gateway/internal/router/platform_routes.go:19,33,50-53`) while the approved table marks the prefix `gone` (`testdata/route_decisions.approved.yaml:21`, `routes_golden_test.go:138-146`). Re-point the subtree to system-setting and update both fixtures; read timeout ≥ 90 s for the chat route.
6. **Tests**: aiclient against `tests/local-stack/mock-ext` `/llm/v1/chat/completions` with `__fail` (`mock_e
pros: Matches the project's own recorded replacement for the retired AI services, so the decom ratchet and conformance tests stay green without amending a baseline
One SSRF/retry/redaction implementation reused by BL-H02 (case-management) and api-test; keys never leave system-setting in clear except over svcauth gRPC
Adds no new runtime component and no new datastore: one MySQL, tables owned by one service (ADR-06)
Uses what already exists: netguard profiles, internal/secret, svcauth, the mock-ext OpenAI endpoint with failure injection
Honest status codes (503/422/502/429) keep ADR-12's "no fake success" intent while retiring the 501
cons: Conflicts with FR-SYS-07 as written ("các hành động chat và chuyển văn bản chưa nối AI phải trả 501 trung thực"): the SRS/URD row must be revised in the same change, which needs the doc owner's approval

Partially conflicts with BRL-64 and ADR-12: a mounted route answering 503 when AI_ENABLED=false is not the "hide entirely, 404 + X-Route-Missing" shape the rule demands; it is a narrow, deliberate exception replacing the existing OI-02 one
Largest option: a new shared package, a new gRPC contract, a migration, gateway fixtures and the FR/ENT doc revision
ENT-17 marks conversation as deferred ("hội thoại (hoãn)") and has no attributes for messages, project scope or usage counters — the entity must gain them
The per-organization cost limit has no number, period or admin surface anywhere in the KG, so this option ships the enforcement point with a configured limit, not a UI

risks.description: The per-org cost limit is invented in the absence of any requirement (unit, period, who sets it, what happens on breach), so it may be reworked once the business answers
Returning the decrypted key over internal gRPC widens the key's blast radius; a misconfigured svcauth caller list or a log of a request body would leak it (NFR-SE-04)
netguard.AdminTarget refuses loopback/private ranges, so the local stack's mock-ext and any on-prem model host need explicit SSRF allow-lists per environment (ADR-15's recorded consequence)
Re-pointing /ai/conversation/* touches gateway golden fixtures and the decom route ledger; a stale fixture fails the conformance gate rather than the feature
DeepSeek/ZhiPu parameter differences from OpenAI are only exercised against a mock; no real provider has been verified in this environment

options.title: Route every model call through the already-deployed LiteLLM proxy and use its budgets
options.summary: Make `ms-llm-proxy` (LiteLLM, already in the dev/dev-remote/production compose files with conf/litellm_config.yaml) the single egress for all model traffic. ms-system-setting keeps declaring sources but issues one LiteLLM virtual key per organization with a `max_budget`, so cost limits and spend accounting come from the proxy; the Go side is a thin OpenAI call to a fixed internal host, netguard FixedHost. Conversation storage, `/ai/conversation/*` and `AI_ENABLED` are still built in system-setting.
options.approach:
**Shape**: keep the Go code minimal and push provider handling, retries, fan-out and budgets into infrastructure that is already declared in `deploy/dev/docker-compose.override.yml:273-286`, `deploy/dev-remote/...` and `deploy/production/conf/litellm_config.yaml` (Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini model list, `router_settings` with `num_retries: 2`, `timeout: 60`).

1. **Egress**: a small `internal/llm` client in ms-system-setting posts `/v1/chat/completions` to `LLM_PROXY_URL` using `netguard.FromEnv(netguard.FixedHost)` with the proxy host allow-listed — the `FixedHost` profile exists for exactly "a third-party endpoint with a known name" (`netguard.go:55-57`). No per-provider code, no provider SDK.
2. **Model sources**: `ai_model_source` rows become a *selection* of proxy-side `model_name` values (`gpt-4o`, `claude-3-5-sonnet`, …). The admin-entered `api_url`/`app_key` are either ignored (the proxy holds provider keys from env) or, in the "BYO key" variant, forwarded to LiteLLM as a passthrough deployment — an ops change in `litellm_config.yaml` plus a redeploy, not a UI action.
3. **Cost limit per organization**: one LiteLLM virtual key per organization, created/rotated by system-setting through LiteLLM's key-management API with `max_budget` + `budget_duration`; the key (not a provider key) is sealed with the existing `internal/secret`. Over-budget is the proxy's 429/400, mapped to a 429 + `Retry-After` for the SPA. Spend reporting comes from LiteLLM, not from a counter we maintain.
4. **Conversations / routes / flag**: same as opt-1 — `V037` migration for `ai_conversation` header + `ai_conversation_message`, `/ai/conversation/*` mounted in system-setting shaped to `ui/tms/src/api/modules/ai.ts`, `AI_ENABLED` gate following `NOTIFICATION_SSE_ENABLED` (`internal/config/config.go:19-20`), and the gateway subtree re-pointed from the retired ai-agent-service proxy to system-setting with its goldens updated.
5. **Ops hardening required before this is production-grade**: `LLM_MASTER_KEY` currently defaults to `sk-dev-local` in the compose override, `deploy/production/conf/litellm_config.yaml` is a copy of the dev file (header still says "Dev"), and LiteLLM needs its own Postgres for keys/budgets/spend — none of which exists in the deploy matrix today.
6. **Tests**: the same mock-ext `/llm/v1/chat/completions` + `__fail` fixtures stand in for the proxy in CI; add a contract test that the Go side never dials a provider host directly (FixedHost refuses anything but the proxy).
pros: Real token and cost accounting plus hard budgets out of the box — the one part of the request the documents do not specify and that opt-1/opt-3 must build by hand
Least Go code: no provider-specific client, no retry/backoff logic of our own, no second secret path for provider keys (they live in the proxy's env)
Single, fixed egress host simplifies SSRF (FixedHost) and any firewall/network policy
Claude and Gemini become reachable without the ErrProviderUnsupported/422 deferral
Provider failover and model aliasing are configuration, not code
cons: Contradicts the project's recorded direction: SOL-P3c-E §3.2 rollout states "Không còn phụ thuộc llm-proxy/Bifrost", and tools/conformance/retired_services.yaml names shared/pkg/aiclient as the replacement for the retired AI services

Hollows out FR-SYS-07 and ENT-17: `api_url`/`app_key` are declared per source by an admin, but with a central proxy an admin can no longer point a source at an arbitrary OpenAI-compatible endpoint without an ops change and redeploy
Conflicts with ADR-06's rationale and shape: LiteLLM needs its own Postgres for virtual keys, budgets and spend, i.e. a second datastore and a table set no service owns in backend/db/ownership.yaml
Secrets split across two stores (internal/secret + LiteLLM master/virtual keys in env and the proxy DB) against NFR-SE-04's single "credential sealed AES-256-GCM, never returned" model
Conflicts with FR-SYS-07's 501 clause and BRL-64/ADR-12 for the AI_ENABLED=false path exactly as opt-1 does, so the doc revision is still needed
Adds a third-party container to the supported production topology, with the dev-shaped config and default master key that implies

risks.description: The production LiteLLM configuration and its datastore do not exist in a reviewed form today (dev file copied, default master key); shipping this makes an unhardened component part of the request path
Reintroducing a dependency the decom ledger retired will be caught by the conformance/port-exposure baselines and needs an explicit amendment by the architecture owner
Per-organization virtual-key lifecycle (create, rotate, revoke, drift between LiteLLM and ai_model_source) is new stateful integration logic with no requirement behind it
Provider-key custody moves to a third-party process, so key redaction and audit guarantees depend on LiteLLM's logging settings rather than our code

options.title: Thin slice inside ms-system-setting only: no shared package, no gRPC contract
options.summary: Deliver a working project-scoped AI chat with the smallest possible surface: an `internal/aiclient` private to ms-system-setting, conversations as header + turns, a per-organization counter, `/ai/conversation/*` behind `AI_ENABLED`, and nothing exported for other services. `/functional/case/ai/*` keeps its honest 501 until BL-H02, which is then responsible for lifting the client into `shared/pkg` and adding the internal contract.
options.approach:
**Shape**: identical behaviour to opt-1 at the HTTP boundary, but everything lives inside one service, so there is no new shared package, no `.proto`, no `svcauth` caller list and no cross-service key handling in this change.

1. **`internal/aiclient`** in `backend/services/platform/system-setting`: one OpenAI-compatible `Chat(ctx, req)` for `Open AI`/`DeepSeek`/`ZhiPu AI`; `Claude`/`Bedrock` ⇒ 422 unsupported. Transport from `netguard.NewClient(netguard.FromEnv(netguard.AdminTarget), 60s)` (`backend/shared/pkg/netguard/netguard.go:41-57`), 2 retries honouring `Retry-After`, key scrubbed from errors/logs (NFR-SE-04), `ai_*` metrics.
2. **Model resolution and keys** stay package-private: reuse `internal/secret.Open` (`internal/secret/secret.go:31`) at call time and the existing `AIConfigUsecase` repository (`internal/usecase/ai/ai.go`) to read `ai_model_source` with the current permission rules (TrimSpace on `owner_type` for the UI's `"SYSTEM "`). The decrypted key never crosses a process boundary in this change.
3. **Project-scoped conversation**: `V037` adds `title`, `scene`, `organization_id`, `project_id`, `model_id`, `update_time` to `ai_conversation` plus `ai_conversation_message`; model choice is per request (`chatModelId` from the SPA) with an optional per-project default column rather than a separate scope-config table. New tables added to `backend/db/ownership.yaml:33` (ADR-06).
4. **Cost limit**: `ai_org_usage(organization_id, period, requests, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost)` incremented in the same transaction as the turn, with the limit read from config (`AI_ORG_MONTHLY_TOKENS`, `AI_ORG_MONTHLY_COST`) until the business defines an admin surface. Over limit ⇒ 429 + `Retry-After`, checked before the provider call.
5. **Routes and flag**: `/ai/conversation/{add,chat,update,list,delete/:id,chat/list/:id}` in `internal/handler/ai/conversation.go`, mounted in `internal/handler/router.go` next to the existing `/ai/config/*` group (lines 354-361), with the idempotent-`add`/upsert-`chat` behaviour the SPA's non-awaited `addChat` requires; `AI_ENABLED` per `internal/config/config.go:19-20`; 503/422/502/429 and never a fake 200.
6. **Gateway**: same single change as opt-1 — move `/ai/conversation/*` off the retired ai-agent-service proxy to system-setting and update `route_decisions.approved.yaml` + `routes_golden_test.go`.
7. **Explicit follow-up written into the change**: BL-H02 must lift `internal/aiclient` to `backend/shared/pkg/aiclient` and add the `AIService` gRPC contract before case-management calls a provider; case-management must not read `ai_model_source` directly (ADR-06).
pros: Smallest blast radius and fastest path to a working, honest AI chat for the SPA that already calls these URLs
No cross-process exposure of a decrypted provider key in this change (the key never leaves the service)
No new shared package or proto to review, so the change is easy to review and to revert
Keeps /functional/case/ai/* at its honest 501, leaving ADR-12's exception untouched for that surface until BL-H02
cons: Diverges from the recorded replacement for the retired AI services (tools/conformance/retired_services.yaml names shared/pkg/aiclient; SOL-P3c-E T-F3-18 specifies the shared package plus the AIService gRPC contract), so BL-H02 pays the refactor
Real risk that BL-H02 shortcuts by reading ai_model_source from case-management, which ADR-06 forbids (one table, one owning service)
Same FR-SYS-07 (501 clause) and BRL-64/ADR-12 (503 on a mounted route) conflicts as opt-1, with the same doc revision needed
Retry/SSRF/redaction logic will have to be duplicated or moved later — the second caller is already planned
Per-org limit is env-configured only; no admin UI, and the limit's semantics remain unspecified by the documents

risks.description: Known rework: the client and the model-resolution contract must be lifted into shared/pkg + gRPC when BL-H02 lands, touching the same files twice
Without the internal contract, a future caller may copy the provider-key read path and weaken the single sealed-secret boundary (NFR-SE-04)
The per-org cost limit is invented against no requirement and may be reworked once the business specifies unit/period/owner
netguard.AdminTarget blocks loopback/private hosts, so local mock-ext and on-prem models need per-environment allow-lists

options.title: Revive the existing ai-agent-service as the AI backend behind /ai/conversation/*
options.summary: ai-agent-service already contains a gRPC chat/transform implementation with an OpenAI client, Redis session store and an agent dispatcher, and the gateway still proxies `/ai/conversation/*` to it. Un-retire the service, harden it (netguard, sealed keys from system-setting, per-org budget, MySQL-persisted conversations) and keep the existing routing. Fastest to a streaming chat, but it reopens a service the project's decommission ledger closed.
options.approach:
**Shape**: use the code that exists instead of writing a new client. `backend/services/ai/ai-agent-service` has `usecases/chat/chat.go` (`StreamChat`, history trimming, GraphRAG context), `usecases/transform/transform.go`, `client/llmproxy/client.go` (go-openai with `LLM_PROXY_URL`/`LLM_MODEL` overrides), `repository/redis/session_store.go` and a generated `proto/ai_agent/v1`. The gateway already has the upstream wired (`internal/router/platform_routes.go:19,33,50-53`).

Work needed to make it acceptable:
1. **Governance first**: remove the `ai-agent-service` entry from `tools/conformance/retired_services.yaml:223-236` and re-approve the `/ai/conversation/*` row in `gateway/internal/router/testdata/route_decisions.approved.yaml:21` (currently `→ gone`), plus the `retiredGone` rows in `routes_golden_test.go:138-146` and the conformance rule that forbids pointing at a retired upstream (`conformance_test.go:1302`), and restore the frozen port-exposure baseline entries.
2. **Delete the fake-success path**: `client/llmproxy/client.go:41-46` falls back to a `noopClient` with "placeholder responses" when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is unset — precisely what ADR-12/BRL-64 forbid and what the non-stub gate greps for. Replace with an honest 503/422.
3. **Real configuration instead of env**: today the model, base URL and key come from process env and the session is hardcoded to `"default_ws"/"default_proj"` (`chat.go:41`). Add a `ResolveModel` call into ms-system-setting over `svcauth` so the admin-declared source, its sealed key (`internal/secret.Open`) and the org/project scope actually drive the call.
4. **SSRF and redaction**: wrap the go-openai transport in `netguard` (`AdminTarget`), scrub keys from errors/logs, add `ai_*` metrics — none of this exists in the service today.
5. **Persistence and budget**: conversations currently live only in Redis (`agent:session:*`); add the MySQL header/turn tables for `GET /ai/conversation/{list,chat/list/:id}` — but those tables belong to system-setting in `backend/db/ownership.yaml:33`, so either the service owns new tables of its own or it calls system-setting (ADR-06). Add the per-organization counter and the pre-call budget check in the same place.
6. **Deploy**: ms-ai-agent-service must be built, released and health-checked in the dev/production compose sets again, and `AI_ENABLED` has to gate both the gateway decision and the service.
pros: Reuses a working gRPC chat/transform implementation, a session store and generated protobufs instead of writing a client from scratch
Streaming chat is already implemented, which the other options defer
The gateway upstream hook for /ai/conversation/* still exists in code, so routing is a config change
cons: Directly against the project's decommission ledger: tools/conformance/retired_services.yaml:223-236 retires ai-agent-service with `replaced_by: F24 chat ở /functional/case/ai/*` and lists /ai/conversation among its retired prefixes; several conformance/golden tests encode that decision
Its current LLM client silently degrades to a placeholder-response noopClient — the fake success ADR-12/BRL-64 and the no-stub gate explicitly forbid
Conflicts with ADR-06: conversation/message tables are owned by system-setting, so either ownership moves or the service needs a cross-service read path
Keeps an extra deployable (plus Redis prefixes and Kafka topics) in the topology for one feature, against ADR-06's "fewer operational components" rationale
Same FR-SYS-07 (501 clause) and BRL-64/ADR-12 AI_ENABLED conflicts as every other option, on top of the un-retirement
Hardening (netguard, sealed keys, scope resolution, redaction, budget, persistence) is most of opt-1's work anyway, so the reuse saving is smaller than it looks

risks.description: Reversing an approved decommission requires amending frozen baselines and golden fixtures; the architecture owner may simply refuse, wasting the work
The service's code quality is demo-level (hardcoded default_ws/default_proj, naive GraphRAG serialisation, env-only config, noopClient fallback) and needs review-grade rework before it faces users
Conversation state split between Redis sessions and MySQL history risks two sources of truth for the same thread
Its GraphRAG/knowledge/case-management clients pull in dependencies on other retired or unrelated AI-track components

Full revert: restore the retired_services.yaml entry, the gateway decision row, the golden fixtures and the port-exposure baseline, stop the service in the compose sets, and drop any tables it added.

recommendation.reason: It is the only option that satisfies the request without fighting the project's own records: the decom ledger (tools/conformance/retired_services.yaml:220) and the solution doc SOL-P3c-E §3.2 (T-F3-18) already name shared/pkg/aiclient + an AIService in ms-system-setting as the replacement for the 501, it keeps keys sealed in one service (NFR-SE-04) behind the netguard AdminTarget profile the documents assign to admin-configured URLs (NFR-SE-05/ADR-15), it adds no datastore or runtime component (ADR-06), and it gives BL-H02 a contract instead of a refactor. Opt-3 is the right fallback if the team wants a smaller first slice and accepts the later lift; opt-2 and opt-4 both require reversing a recorded decommission decision.

assumptions.text: "Nguồn mô hình tương thích OpenAI" means the three providers the SPA can create (Open AI, DeepSeek, ZhiPu AI per ui/tms/src/enums/modelEnum.ts); Claude/Bedrock stay deferred and answer 422 unsupported rather than being stubbed.

"Hội thoại AI theo dự án" means a conversation row carries organization_id/project_id and model resolution may be overridden per project; the SPA today sends only organizationId, so the project level is stored and resolvable but no UI change ships in this request.
AI_ENABLED is an application-level kill switch on mounted routes (503 when off), following the existing NOTIFICATION_SSE_ENABLED precedent, not a route-mount switch returning 404 + X-Route-Missing.

The per-organization cost limit is enforced in-platform from the token usage the provider reports, counted per organization per calendar period, with the limit supplied by configuration until an admin surface is specified.
services/infrastructure/integration-hub is not touched (protected per CLAUDE.md), and /functional/case/ai/{chat,transform} keeps its honest 501 in this request (BL-H02 owns it).
The FR-SYS-07 / ENT-17 revision and the BRL-64 exception are published as part of this change via the normal document-change path, not assumed silently.

open_questions.text: What exactly is the per-organization cost limit: unit (tokens, requests or currency), period (daily/monthly), who sets it (super-admin, org admin, env) and what the API returns on breach? Nothing in the knowledge graph states it; NFR-PE-07 covers HTTP rate limits only.

Does AI_ENABLED=false answering 503 on a mounted route get an explicit, recorded exception to BRL-64/ADR-12 (which demand 404 + X-Route-Missing for a feature that is off), or must the routes be unmounted when the flag is off?

What marks one ai_model_source as "the system default" that project/organization resolution falls back to (a dedicated flag, or the oldest enabled PUBLIC source)? ENT-17's attributes do not include one.

Is sending project data (case text, prompts) to an externally hosted model permitted, and are there data-residency or logging restrictions? No Decision, Constraint or QualityTarget in the graph covers outbound prompt content.
Is streaming (/ai/conversation/stream/...) in scope? The SPA declares it but the current chat call is non-streaming, and no element in the graph requires streaming.

Which environments get AI enabled by default, and may the local stack point a model source at the mock-ext loopback endpoint (which requires an explicit netguard allow-host, ADR-15's recorded consequence)?

gaps: No element specifies the per-organization AI cost limit (unit, period, owner, breach response), the AI_ENABLED flag, a system-default model source, or whether streaming is required. ENT-17 still marks conversation as deferred ("hội thoại (hoãn)") and has no message, project-scope or usage-counter attributes; the typed gap and drift queries returned no rows, so these are my findings, not a recorded gap list.
conflicts: FR-SYS-07 requires that chat/transform answer an honest 501 while AI is unwired, so every option contradicts its current text (SRS line:432, URD line:1357) and needs the requirement revised with the change.

BRL-64 and ADR-12 require a feature that is off to be hidden entirely (404 + X-Route-Missing, "không được có route 501 hoặc 200 giả"); a mounted route answering 503 when AI_ENABLED=false is a narrow exception replacing the existing AI 501 exception (OI-02). Opt-2 additionally conflicts with ADR-06 (LiteLLM needs its own datastore outside the single owned-table MySQL) and opt-4 ships ADR-12's forbidden fake success (noopClient placeholder replies).
